father hegarty’s rock only three weeks after his installation as bishop of derry, the most reverend michael router paid a pas- toral visit last sunday to the parishes of burt, inch & fahan and desertegney & lower fahan (buncrana). we were delighted to have him amongst us on what was an unseasonably warm and sunny day, for what was a spectacularly wonderful occasion. he walked with us on a synodal walk from the stone jug and cele- brated mass on father hegarty’s rock , before returning then to cockhill parish hall for tea and refreshments. the turnout was splendid, the welcome warm, the sup- port immense and the faith tangible. in the midst of a sometimes stiff atlantic breeze he joked about not be-ing blown into the water, seemingly perched as he was on the edge of the lough. but from there he com- manded a great view of the gathering and the statue of friar seamus hegarty op – and he offered a most memorable mass recalling the courage and hope which father hegarty had in abundance, and asking god to grant us the same gifts for the challenges in our own time. the music and singing were outstanding and the joy and contentment of those gathered there, of all ages, was clear to be seen. after visiting father walsh in his home, the bishop returned to derry with a spring in his step and firm in the knowledge that he will always be welcome in these parts. it was a truly wonderful occasion made possible only by the devotion and help of huge teams of people: our stewards and volunteers, choirs and musicians, farmers and bakers, schools and parents’ associations (especially at st oran’s ns ), and to all who came to celebrate. to them all and to god himself, we must always be thankful. father bradley station masses have resumed in the month of october ardmore parish newsletter twenty-ninth sunday in ordinary time – year a sunday, 18th october 2026 gospel reflection (matthew 22:15–21) in today’s gospel, religious leaders try to trap jesus with a question about paying taxes to caesar. pointing to the coin’s image and inscription, he teaches us to fulfil our earthly responsibilities while giving our deepest allegiance to god. jesus reminds us that not every question deserves a fight. what matters is whether our choices reflect goodness, truth, and love, drawing us closer to god, strengthening our character, and blessing others. a life well lived is measured not by arguments won, but by faithfulness to god’s will. the coin carried caesar’s image, reminding us to respect legitimate laws, perform our duties honestly, support our families, and contribute positively to society. faith does not excuse us from responsible citizenship; it inspires us to fulfil our duties with sincerity and fairness. the coin bore caesar’s image, but our lives are called to reflect god’s goodness. though we cannot do so perfectly every day, we can choose to grow: let our words encourage, our hands help, and our hearts forgive. we may give money to the world, time to our responsibilities, and attention to our ambitions, but we must give god what belongs to him: our love, worship, gratitude, trust, and obedience. our relationship with god remains the foundation of a meaningful life. we may carry coins in our pockets, but we carry god’s calling in our hearts. give the world your honest service, others your genuine love, and god your whole heart. that is how an ordinary life becomes a beautiful offering to him. world mission sunday october has been the month of universal mission since 1926. mission sunday invites catholics to unite with missionaries worldwide and recommit to the church’s missionary activity through prayer, sacrifice and financial support. ardmore

funds help young churches and missionaries serve communities in need, both spiritually and materially. contributions build mission churches, educate seminarians, form catechists and lay leaders, fund children’s health clinics, provide emergency aid in war or disaster, and help missionaries care for refugees. this year’s theme is ‘one in christ, united in mission’ . today we celebrate our approximately 1,500 irish-born missionaries and all missionaries worldwide, thanking god for them, for those who support them at home, and for our growing communion with them and the communities they serve. to read pope leo’s message for world mission sunday, please visit the official world mission sunday 2026 message. readings for sunday, 25th october first reading: exodus 22:20– 26 psalm: psalm 18:2–3, 3–4, 47, 51 second reading: 1 thessalonians 1:5c– 10 gospel: matthew 22:34– 40 saints of the coming week monday, 19th october st john de brébeuf, st isaac jogues, priests and companions, martyrs st paul of the cross, priest thursday, 22nd october st john paul pope friday, 23rd october st john of capistrano, priest saturday, 24th october st anthony mary claret, bishop annual day of prayer, praise and healing sunday, 15th november 2026 – silver birch hotel, omagh
